rationale:
Evidence: all six designs ended off-track in all 60 trials. max_error sits at 0.061 to 0.066 m against the 0.06 m limit, and rms_error is about 0.03 m whatever the gain. Gain changes (kp 1.2 to 3), speed changes (0.8 to 1.6) and span changes (+/-0.032 to +/-0.06 m) have all failed to move the failure point. Iterations 3, 5 and 6 produced nearly identical oval metrics (progress 0.1675, max_error 0.066) despite different kp, ki, kd, mass and sensor span. The failure therefore looks insensitive to the parameters I have tried, so the next draft should test a different factor, not another gain sweep.

Changes: (1) Sensor span narrowed to x = -0.03 to +0.03 in 0.01 m steps (7 sensors, 12 mm footprints), with y = 0.06. This tests whether the robot is reacting to readings from the outer sensors at the edge of the band. (2) Weights set to x/0.04 (-0.75, -0.5, -0.25, 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75), which keeps the signal slope near 25 per metre, the same as iteration 5, so the controller gain per metre of offset is unchanged. (3) kp 1.6, ki 0.3, kd 1.0 and base_speed 0.9, held close to the best-scoring run (iteration 5 and 3). (4) Mass 0.4 and wheel_track 0.14, wheel_radius 0.03 and body unchanged. line_loss stays last_direction.

Expected result: max_error still near 0.06, since this is a diagnostic. If the excursion shrinks, the outer-sensor edge is the driver. If nothing changes, the next step is to change the drivetrain geometry (wheel_track or wheel_radius) because the controller has not moved the outcome.
